Order
Appellant-insurance company is aggrieved of the award dated 28.01.2004 passed in Motor Accident Claim Case No.221/2001 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Satna (for short, "the Tribunal") in allowing Rs.55,000/- along with interest and cost as compensation in favour of respondent no.1-claimant.

2. Brief facts are that on 10.03.2001 respondent no.1-claimant was walking down with Kunwarlal to his village Pawaiya when they both were hit by a Commander Jeep bearing registration no.MP-19-A-9248 whose driver was driving it rashly and negligently.

It was claimed that respondent no.1- claimant sustained grievous injuries and permanent disability on account of accident and,
therefore, a claim petition for Rs.19,09,000/- was filed which NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:10622 2 MA-1268-2004 was partially allowed by the Tribunal.
3. Appellant-insurance company contested the claim by questioning the accident itself.

According to it, the name of vehicle which caused accident could not be ascertained despite detailed investigation and, therefore, a closure report was filed by police regarding the FIR lodged with respect to the Oriental Insurance Comp.Ltd. vs Ramesh Prasad Raikwar & Anr on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127162080/
1 alleged accident.

sentences.text: Same are the contentions of appellant before this appellate court and it is submitted that under a collusion between respondent no.1-claimant and respondent no.2, the owner of vehicle, the claim petition was filed with manipulative implant of his vehicle in the accident.
4. Appeal is strongly contested by respondent no.1-claimant.
5. Counsel for both the parties have been heard and record of the Tribunal has been examined.

6. A bare perusal of claim petition itself reflects that respondent no.1- claimant was well aware of the fact that no final charge-sheet in the alleged accident case was filed by the police, as para 5 of claim petition makes an admission to the fact that a closure report was filed by police.
It is strange that despite being a victim of an alleged criminal act of rash and negligent driving, respondent no.1-claimant did not prefer any complaint case before a criminal court.
If the wrongdoer of a criminal act was ascertained, it was expected of the victim of said act to file a criminal complaint particularly when police was not taking any action against that wrongdoer.
Instead of taking that measure, respondent no.1-claimant chose to file only a case for damages for tortuous act and this inaction makes his claim petition questionable.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10622 3 MA-1268-2004 7.

From the record of criminal case it is revealed that police was informed on 11.03.2001 regarding the accident which occurred on 10.03.2001 and the FIR against an unknown driver of Commander Jeep was registered on 13.03.2001.

Ex.P-3 is the closure report dated 24.12.2001 and it makes it clear that by the time it was prepared, the unknown driver was not traced and even the registration number of offending vehicle could not be ascertained.

In terms of these facts the statements of alleged eyewitness of accident, namely Ramcharan Singh (A.W.3), become highly unreliable wherein he claims that he was in acquaintance with respondent no.1-claimant and had noted the registration number of offending vehicle while witnessing the accident.
He further claims that the registration number of offending vehicle was communicated to the father of respondent no.1-claimant.
Another eyewitness Ashok Singh (A.W.6) is the son of witness Ramcharan Singh (A.W.3).
He too claims that he was along with his father at the scene of incident and had informed the father of respondent no.1-claimant about the accident.

It is unbelievable that despite receiving such immediate information from a close acquaintance, respondent no.1-claimant or his family members failed to give information of the registration number or the driver of offending vehicle to the police during a long period of investigation of almost nine months and also failed to file any complaint case for the criminal act of driver of alleged vehicle.
8. In terms of facts discussed above, it can be gathered that only at a subsequent stage with the connivance of owner of offending vehicle, namely respondent no.2, the claim petition was filed.

The Tribunal, while deciding NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10622 4 MA-1268-2004 issue no.1, was impressed by the fact that vehicle owner-driver had admitted the accident in his written statement, but it ignored the important defence of appellant-insurance company, that there was a collusion between the vehicle owner-driver and respondent no.1-claimant.

This argument of collusion is fortified with the fact that respondent no.1-claimant did not chose to prosecute and seek Oriental Insurance Comp.Ltd. vs Ramesh Prasad Raikwar & Anr on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127162080/
2 punishment for respondent no.2-owner-cum-driver of the offending vehicle for his criminal liability and has also not given any explanation for this deliberate inaction.
9.

sentences.text: In all these cases it was held that a criminal case cannot be decided solely on the basis of documents forming part of police record or the result of police investigation or even the fate of criminal trial, and the only standard of proof to be applied by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal is the preponderance of probabilities and not the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt.
Incidentally, this appellate Court is not deciding the dispute solely on the basis of result of criminal investigation.
In none of these judgments cited by respondent no.1, the Courts expressed the view that the criminal record should be entirely overlooked as irrelevant piece of evidence.

Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sithara N. S. and others, etc. v.
Sai Ram NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10622 5 MA-1268-2004 General Insurance Company Limited (Civil Appeal Nos.14718-14719 of 2025, decided on 12.12.2025) has adopted a balanced approach by observing that criminal case documents cannot be viewed in isolation but in conjunction with other infirmities in the evidence produced before the claims tribunal and it further observed that tragic loss suffered by the families of deceased in an accident case is immeasurable,
however, the principles of law cannot be set aside on the ground of sympathy alone and the liability under Motor Vehicles Act must be established through credible evidence.

sentences.text: In other words, a holistic view of entire evidence has to be taken into consideration and claimants have to establish the case on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and not on the strict proof of liabilities.

10. The meticulous appreciation of evidence reflects that present case is not the one, in which there was any delay in FIR or the registration number of the offending vehicle was communicated to the police.

It is a case where identity of the vehicle was never ascertained during the investigation and suddenly out of nowhere the claim was filed by alleging that accident was caused by a particular vehicle and a particular person.
There was complete inaction on the part of respondent no.1 to initiate proceedings against wrongdoer under criminal jurisprudence.
The eyewitnesses in the case are mistrustful and unworthy of any credit.

Therefore, in the facts of the case, it unfolds that respondent no.1-claimant has down rightly failed to prove that alleged accident was caused by offending vehicle bearing registration No. MP-19-A-9248.
11.

Having considered the facts and legal aspects involved in the case, this NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:10622 6 MA-1268-2004 appeal is allowed and the appellant-insurance company is exonerated from payment of any compensation amount to respondent no.1-claimant.
12. Appeal is accordingly allowed and disposed of.
13. Let a copy of this order along with record be sent back to the concerned Tribunal for information and necessary compliance.
